TITLE: Replace the bare import Mathlib in 86 modules by precise imports
SUMMARY:
The dominant build cost, and the method is now settled. 86 of 164 modules opened with a bare 'import Mathlib'; measured on Cohomology/SheafCompose.lean (49 lines), 16.6 s and about 7 GB with the umbrella versus 3.5 s and 1.97 GB with four precise imports. ORDERING RULE, learned the expensive way. Bottom-up is right for probe CORRECTNESS -- a module's minimal imports cannot be computed until everything beneath it is clean -- but wrong for NET PROGRESS whenever the module has a cone of import-less dependents above it. Narrowing StructureSheafModuleK/Presheaf.lean stripped the library from nine modules in the StructureSheafModuleK -> Genus -> Jacobian chain. Give a module's import-less dependents their own precise imports FIRST, top-down within the cone, then narrow the parent.

They are invisible to the minimal-import probe because nothing in their own text says what they need, and every one that gets its own imports permanently removes a class of breakage. Elaborating all 54 in parallel with 'lake env lean' (read-only against .lake/build, safe alongside a running build) resolves the whole exposure in minutes; a full build finds only one victim per round because lake stops at the first failure in a chain.
